# Termux-BitNet Full Technical Specification (v1.0.0)
Official Documentation & Deep Architecture Reference for Autonomous AI Agents.

## 1. System Overview
High-Performance 1.58-bit (i2_s) BitNet On-Device LLM Inference Runtime for ARM64 & Android Termux
Engineered with a single C++17 core utilizing ARM64 NEON DotProd (vdotq_s32) SIMD instructions and dual lightweight thin gateways (Python ctypes FFI and Node.js CLI IPC), delivering low-latency 1.58-bit ternary quantized LLM execution directly on device memory without background server daemons.

## 2. Package & Installation
- PyPI: termux-bitnet
- Command: pip install termux-bitnet
# or: npm install termux-bitnet
- Repository: https://github.com/uno-km/termux-bitnet

## 3. Core Capabilities
- **ARM64 NEON & DotProd Acceleration**: Native SIMD assembly kernels (vdotq_s32 and vmlal_s8 fallback) providing high throughput integer dot product computation on mobile processors.
- **Single Core & Dual Thin Gateways**: All heavy compute is consolidated in pure C++ libtermux_bitnet.so, while Python and Node.js serve as thin, zero-overhead entry gateways.
- **Zero-Daemon Direct Execution**: Runs in-process via direct C ABI calls without requiring background server daemons, port listeners, or network socket layers.
- **Ternary Weight (i2_s) Quantization**: Consumes only 1.58 bits per parameter (-1, 0, +1), reducing model storage and memory bandwidth footprint by up to 70% compared to 8-bit models.
- **Verified Model Registry Downloader**: Built-in automated download engine supporting official Microsoft and community BitNet GGUF models with automatic HTTP range resume.

## 4. Canonical Implementation
```python
from termux_bitnet import BitNetEngine, BitNetConfig

# 1. Configure engine parameters
config = BitNetConfig(
    model_path="~/.cache/termux-bitnet/models/bitnet-2b-ggml-model-i2_s.gguf",
    n_threads=8,
    temperature=0.7,
    top_p=0.95,
    top_k=40,
    repeat_penalty=1.15
)

# 2. Stream generation directly from ARM64 C++ core
with BitNetEngine(config) as engine:
    for token in engine.generate_stream("Summarize the architectural benefit of 1.58-bit weights:"):
        print(token, end="", flush=True)

```
